premises.text: Home robots must become engaging, affordable, and fun like personal computers rather than large expensive machines
premises.evidence_span: move them into engaging, affordable, and fun to use robots in the home

premises.text: Smartphone and cloud robotics shift computation off the robot so it is cheaper and dynamically upgradable
premises.evidence_span: smartphone robotics and cloud robotics that takes a computation from the robot into devices you already have, making it much more affordable

premises.text: Targeted limited-task robots that do simple things well can enter homes affordably before later combining
premises.evidence_span: a set of robots that are much more targeted at limited set of tasks

premises.text: Shimmy is a speaker-dog whose intelligence runs on phone/cloud while hardware is motors, speakers, and power, enabling music-reactive choreography and face tracking
premises.evidence_span: everything that the robot does actually happens on a smartphone app and on the cloud

premises.text: Consumer price point around $199, with early Kickstarter at $149
premises.evidence_span: we're able to get it to $199

value.text: An affordable, fun smartphone-powered robot in every home
value.evidence_span: the promise of a robot in every home and make it a reality

notes: PC analogy and Swiss-army vs targeted robots kept as strategy premises with smartphone/cloud enabling claim. Music choreography, mood play, and face tracking folded into dumb-robot/smartphone mechanism (§4.1.7). Future kitchen/car concepts treated as roadmap vision not premises (§4.1.4). Kickstarter price kept as commercial packaging. Demo failures noted but not coded.
